title: Highbury Stadium
subtitle: Perhaps he never came out of that fog.

items.text: Highbury Stadium
I'm afraid of the fog.
That's right, the Fogwalker responsible for dealing with London's fog problem is in fact terrified by it. Is there anything in the world more ironic than that?
I'm afraid of this thick fog that devours everything—voices, wishes, fate... Even that majestic figure ended up being swallowed whole by the fog...
That was when I was a child—before I became the Fogwalker.
My mother turned her head for only a second, and I snuck out of the house. I wanted to embark on a great journey, and my destination was Highbury Stadium.
Arsenal was the best team in London at the time, and every child in London dreamt of becoming a player. I was no exception.
I wanted to go there, to Highbury Stadium and join the team.
I was fantasizing about running around Highbury in a full Arsenal kit, imitating the movements of the players, completely oblivious to the fact that I had deviated from my path.
That was when the fog came.
First, a thin and almost invisible mist began to suffuse the air.
It was like a clever thief, stealing all sense of direction and setting me on the wrong path.
Then another wave of thick fog came rushing in that completely obscured my view.
With a wicked smile, it set me apart from my dreams. It told me that I would never go anywhere—ever again, that I would remain in this dense fog for my whole life.
Finally, that dreadful, clinging, sticky dark fog arrived.
It destroyed the last remaining sliver of my courage, imprisoning me where I stood, leaving me unable to move so that all I could do was stand there, crying and praying.
Yet, no matter how much I cried, my voice couldn't penetrate through the dense and clinging air.
After destroying my dreams and my courage, at the last it stripped me of my fragile rights as a human.
The fog gradually turned black from end to end. It sought to rob this cage I was in of its last remaining light. It wanted me to fear it—to fear it as though it were fear itself.
That pitch-black, brutal fog—hung just the way it does now.

items.speaker: Oliver Fog
items.text: Why are there so many critters? Something's entirely wrong here!

items.speaker: A Knight
items.text: Someone did tell you that this forest was not safe at night, Mr. Fog.

items.speaker: A Knight
items.text: The Fogwalker pauses for a moment, then came to a sudden realization.

items.speaker: Oliver Fog
items.text: So that's why you're here... You came to protect me?

items.speaker: A Knight
items.text: No, of course not! Someone simply came here to play the part of a talking tree.

items.speaker: Oliver Fog
items.text: ...I've caused you nothing but trouble, Mr. Knight. Please accept my apology. My stubbornness dragged you into this mess, and I feel just awful about it...

items.speaker: A Knight
items.text: You're the second person to apologize to someone today, and someone's response is still the same. There's no need for apologies, Sir Oliver.

items.speaker: Oliver Fog
items.text: I've never seen this many critters before in my life... It's beyond me.
The indistinct mass of shadows piled together surrounds the two of them.

items.speaker: Oliver Fog
items.text: Critters cover every inch of ground a meter away from them in all directions, trapping the two of them where they stand.

items.speaker: A Knight
items.text: Are you trembling, Sir Oliver?

items.speaker: Oliver Fog
items.text: ...They're just like that cloying black fog—a wicked pitch-dark mass that seems to have no end.

items.speaker: Oliver Fog
items.text: Fog... A heavy dense fog... A terrifying fog from which not even light can permeate.

items.speaker: A Knight
items.text: Are you afraid, sir? Would you show fear to the enemy standing before you?

items.speaker: Oliver Fog
items.text: ...Anyone would be afraid to face this many enemies all at once.
Countless critters fold in around the two of them. Blending into the dark forest, making it impossible to distinguish their type as they approach.

items.speaker: Oliver Fog
items.text: The swarm seems endless, emerging incessently from the depths of the forest, expanding and filling the space around them.
But for some unknown reason, they refrain from launching their attack, instead simply forming an ever thickening ring.

items.speaker: A Knight
items.text: Hah! This reminds someone of the battlefield someone once stood in mere moments before being slain in combat.

items.speaker: A Knight
items.text: Someone was surrounded by an equally large number of enemies then... No, indeed, take heart- there were perhaps a dozens times more than this.

items.speaker: Oliver Fog
items.text: ...Mr. Knight, it's all because of me that you've had to put your life in danger once more.

items.speaker: Oliver Fog
items.text: I take full responsibility for my actions, good sir, and I shall do everything I can to help you escape.
The young man takes a deep breath and opens his umbrella once more, preparing to take on the endless dark mist. However, his trembling hands and legs betray him.

items.speaker: Oliver Fog
items.text: There's simply no way we can handle this many enemies...

items.speaker: Oliver Fog
items.text: The only thing I take solace in now is the fact that at least Miss Vertin was aware of my intentions...

items.speaker: Oliver Fog
items.text: Now, all we can do is pray that Miss Vertin realizes the two of us are missing and comes looking for us...

items.speaker: Oliver Fog
items.text: The Fogwalker's voice trembles slightly.

items.speaker: A Knight
items.text: Hah, someone has remembered something rather fitting.

items.speaker: A Knight
items.text: Someone once had a close friend with the exact same name as your own.

items.speaker: A Knight
items.text: That name used to be one which someone often called. Someone went through countless challenges with this friend—sharing both glories and suffering together.

items.speaker: A Knight
items.text: Back in those days, someone was but a reckless boy, but thanks to that friend, someone was able to grow into a true and worthy knight.

items.speaker: A Knight
items.text: He saved someone's life several times too, even though someone dragged him into trouble on countless occasions. When someone looks back on it now, someone cannot help but feel remorseful.

items.speaker: A Knight
items.text: Sorry, this rusty old armor is full of useless memories from long ago.

items.speaker: A Knight
items.text: You and someone's old confidant are indeed very similar. Every time someone sees you, someone can't help but think of those adventures from a past life.

items.speaker: A Knight
items.text: He was an excellent, intelligent, and level-headed fellow, just like you.

items.speaker: Oliver Fog
items.text: ...Are you having a laugh at me?

items.speaker: A Knight
items.text: Someone's command of irony as a rhetorical device is far less sophisticated than the perfect proficiency you modern Britons seem to possess. Perhaps you should learn to have a more faith in yourself...

items.speaker: A Knight
items.text: Although you are still just a child and immature in many ways, one day, someone is sure, you will also become a great knight like he was.

items.speaker: Oliver Fog
items.text: But I am no knight.

items.speaker: A Knight
items.text: Someone remembers you saying only this morning that knights were a thing of the past. Perhaps your musings hold some truth; however, someone believes that the spirit of chivalry shall never die.

items.speaker: A Knight
items.text: And you truly do have the spark of potential to become a knight.

items.speaker: Oliver Fog
items.text: It's a nice sentiment, but I'll never be an Arsenal player or a knight. Being a Fogwalker is my sole calling.

items.speaker: Oliver Fog
items.text: Just like my father, and his father before him, and his father before him... This is the fate of all the Fogs.

items.speaker: Oliver Fog
items.text: All my hopes and dreams are trapped, never to be set free... Trapped in that unconquerable fog.

items.speaker: A Knight
items.text: Unconquerable, eh...?

items.speaker: A Knight
items.text: There is nothing in this world that is truly unconquerable, Oliver.

items.speaker: Oliver Fog
items.text: ...That notion certainly is pleasing to hear at the moment.

items.speaker: Oliver Fog
items.text: But if things were the way you said they were, why would you—

items.speaker: Oliver Fog
items.text: ...Sorry, I've let my emotions get the better of me.

items.speaker: A Knight
items.text: Death may be an end, but it's not the end for us, Oliver.

items.speaker: A Knight
items.text: How about someone tells you the story of Oliver in kind for your bravely speaking about your father?

items.speaker: A Knight
items.text: Someone's closest friend... The story of Oliver, the Knight.

items.speaker: Oliver Fog
items.text: What happened to him?

items.speaker: Oliver Fog
items.text: ...I apologize, Sir Knight... I'm asking pointless questions.

items.speaker: A Knight
items.text: He died.

items.speaker: A Knight
items.text: And it seems he was not as lucky as someone else. He was not granted the gift of returning to the world, born into a new identity.

items.speaker: A Knight
items.text: But he'll never truly die.
TO BE CONTINUED ...
